- 1) Immediate neurology evaluation for suspected demyelinating process (left arm numbness/weakness with sensory changes and transient visual disturbance). Arrange urgent neurology referral with brain imaging (MRI). No medications started at this visit; steroids may be considered by neurology if an acute demyelinating attack is diagnosed.

  - Vision disturbance occurred a few weeks ago, lasted ~20 minutes, resolved spontaneously.

Objective:
- Physical exam findings: Not documented in transcript.

- Investigations: No tests or results performed at this visit.

Assessment & Plan:

1) Left upper extremity numbness with subjective weakness and sensory changes (2nd–4th fingers, palmar side)
- Assessment: Possible demyelinating process (suspicion for multiple sclerosis) vs other etiologies (cervical radiculopathy, boxing-related injury, peripheral neuropathy).
- Differential diagnoses: Multiple sclerosis; cervical radiculopathy; boxing-related nerve/soft-tissue injury; other central or peripheral neuropathies; transient ischemic event unlikely but considered.
- Investigations planned: Urgent neurology referral with brain MRI as part of diagnostic workup.
- Treatment planned: No medications started today; management contingent on neurology assessment. Steroids may be considered if an acute demyelinating attack is diagnosed.
- Referrals: Urgent neurology referral for advanced evaluation and brain imaging.

2) Transient left-eye vision disturbance
- Assessment: Possible demyelinating event (optic involvement) in the context of suspected demyelinating disease; requires neurology evaluation.
- Differential diagnoses: Optic neuritis; demyelinating optic involvement; other transient visual disturbances.
- Investigations planned: Included in neurology referral; brain imaging (MRI) as part of evaluation.
- Treatment planned: None at this visit; treatment decisions to be guided by neurology findings.
- Referrals: Included with neurology referral (see above).

3) Neck pain (background symptom)
- Assessment: Non-specific neck pain; may relate to musculoskeletal strain or cervical involvement in context of neurological symptoms.
- Investigations planned: To be determined by neurology evaluation.
- Treatment planned: Not initiated at this visit; rely on neurology assessment.
- Referrals: Neurology referral will address this symptom as part of overall evaluation.
